In Laravel, you write an observer class with methods named `creating`, `updating` or `deleting` (which fire before the write), and `HasEvents` registers it via `observe()` or the `#[ObservedBy]` attribute and fires those events. `ObservedBy.php` defines the attribute, and `ArtisanServiceProvider.php` provides the `make:observer` scaffolding command, which is supporting rather than essential.

`HasEvents.php` provides `observe()`, which registers an observer class for each method it defines whose name matches a model event (such as `creating`, `updating`, `deleting`), so those methods run before the change. `ObserverMakeCommand.php` generates that observer class, `Dispatcher.php` is the event bus that invokes the registered listeners, and `ModelInspector.php` reads the registered observers back for inspection.

`AbstractRouteCollection` decides the outcome when no route matches: `checkForAlternateVerbs()` retries the other verbs in `Router::$verbs`, and if any match it throws `MethodNotAllowedHttpException` (405) or, for an OPTIONS request, returns a synthetic 200 response with an `Allow` header, otherwise it throws `NotFoundHttpException` (404). `CompiledRouteCollection::match()` is the Symfony-compiled matcher entry point that falls back to this logic, and `Router.php` defines the verb list (line 136) that the alternate-verb check iterates over.

`AbstractRouteCollection.php` does the work: when no route matches, `checkForAlternateVerbs()` tries the other verbs in `Router::$verbs`. If any match, `getRouteForMethods()` returns a synthetic 200 response with an `Allow` header for OPTIONS, or throws `MethodNotAllowedHttpException` for other verbs. If none match, it throws `NotFoundHttpException`. `CompiledRouteCollection.php` is the production matcher that falls through to this logic when the compiled matcher finds nothing. `Router.php` defines the verb list and the `options()` registration.

`AbstractRouteCollection` holds the logic: when no route matches the request's verb, `handleMatchedRoute` calls `checkForAlternateVerbs` to test the other verbs in `Router::$verbs`. If any match, it throws `MethodNotAllowedHttpException` (405) with the allowed verbs, unless the request is `OPTIONS`, in which case `getRouteForMethods` returns a synthetic route that answers 200 with an `Allow` header. If nothing matches under any verb, it throws `NotFoundHttpException` (404). `RouteCollection::match` is the entry point that runs this for the uncompiled collection, `CompiledRouteCollection::match` handles the cached-route path and falls back to it, and `Router.php` defines the verb list and the `options()` registration.
